convocation

kon-vuh-KAY-shuhn · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Convocation is a large, formal assembly of people.

Robes rustled through the auditorium as the graduating class filed in for the university's spring convocation.

Worked Example

The archbishop opened the annual convocation by welcoming delegates who had traveled from every diocese in the country.

Convocation names both the act of calling people together and the formal gathering itself, usually for a ceremony or important announcement.

Your Turn

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

assembly: An assembly is any sizable group brought together on purpose — a school assembly, a town assembly — and it is the plain, general word. A convocation is one particular kind of assembly: formally summoned for a ceremony or official occasion, with the weight of ritual attached.

gathering: A gathering is the loosest of these words: any coming-together, from a backyard barbecue to a crowd on a corner. A convocation is never casual — it is large, formally called, and ceremonial, the kind of occasion that comes with robes, programs, and an official summons.

congregation: A congregation is a community gathered for worship — the regular faithful of a church, synagogue, or mosque at prayer. A convocation, even a religious one, is a formal, summoned assembly for a ceremony or council, like delegates called together, not a congregation's weekly service.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

dispersal: the act of scattering or spreading apart

isolation: the state of being alone or separated from others

Where it sits · how much weight the gathering carries — meeting → convocation → summit

meeting vs. convocation: A meeting can be as small as two people, without the scale or formality of a full convocation.

summit vs. convocation: A summit goes beyond an ordinary convocation, typically bringing together the very top leaders to make major decisions.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — con-

prefix — con-: with, together (Latin)

root — voc-

root — voc-: to call (Latin vocare)

suffix — -ation

suffix — -ation: the act or result of; forms a noun (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin con- ('together') plus vocare ('to call') plus the noun suffix -ation: literally 'a calling together.' The same voc- root is behind the everyday word vocal.

Use the root in a new word: vocal

Use the root in a new word: vocal: The crowd grew increasingly vocal as the referee's calls kept going against the home team.

Root Check

Word Choice

Convocation almost always describes a ceremonial or official gathering -- a graduation, a religious council, a formal academic assembly -- rather than an everyday meeting.
